title: How many numbers from 21 to 30 are prime, and how many composite?
description: The ten numbers from twenty one to thirty are tested one by one by listing a factor pair, and the board sorts them into prime and composite. Keeko doubts the sorting and says that all the odd numbers are prime.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number with exactly two factors is prime, a number with more than two factors is composite, and one factor pair other than one and the number is enough to make it composite. Watch for students who call every odd number prime.

source: How many prime numbers are there from 21 to 30? How many com
video_script.why: The child sorts the numbers from twenty one to thirty by looking for a factor other than one and the number itself, and counts the primes and the composites.
video_script.substitution: Look for a factor pair other than one and the number for each of the ten numbers.
video_script.anchor: A strip of the ten numbers from 21 to 30 on the board
video_script.wrong_answer: all the odd numbers are prime
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko calls every odd number prime. The odd number twenty five is five times five, and twenty one is three times seven, so each has more than two factors and is composite.
video_script.payoff_line: From twenty one to thirty, two numbers are prime and eight are composite.

final_answer.spoken: two are prime and eight are composite

maths_rules: 23 has only the factors 1 and 23; 29 has only the factors 1 and 29
slip: 21, 25 and 27 are odd but composite
video_script.design: The ten numbers sit in a strip; each gets a factor pair beside it and turns amber when a pair other than one and itself is found.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a strip of the numbers 21 to 30; two boxes labelled prime and composite

marks.strip: the strip of ten numbers appears
marks.boxes: the two boxes appear below the strip

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the numbers after twenty.
<bookmark mark='strip'/>Look at the ten numbers from twenty one to thirty.
<bookmark mark='boxes'/>How many of them are prime, and how many are composite?

beats.on_screen: the strip and the two boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Three cards: exactly two factors = prime; more than two factors = composite; 1 has one factor = neither
narration: <bookmark mark='prime'/>A number with exactly two factors, one and itself, is a prime number.
<bookmark mark='comp'/>A number with more than two factors is a composite number.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The number one has only one factor, so it is neither prime nor composite.

marks.given: the ten numbers are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the ten numbers from twenty one to thirty.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many are prime, how many are composite

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many are prime and how many are composite.

marks.even: the five even numbers are picked out
marks.pair: each even number gets a factor pair with two

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Step one, take the even numbers. Twenty two, twenty four, twenty six, twenty eight and thirty are even.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>Two divides each of them. Twenty two, for example, is two times eleven.
<bookmark mark='comp'/>That makes five more than two factors, so all five are composite.

beats.on_screen: Odd numbers: 21 = 3 × 7 composite; 23 factors 1, 23 prime; 25 = 5 × 5 composite; 27 = 3 × 9 composite; 29 factors 1, 29 prime

marks.odd: the five odd numbers are picked out
marks.pairs: twenty one, twenty five and twenty seven get factor pairs and turn amber
marks.primes: twenty three and twenty nine turn teal

narration: <bookmark mark='odd'/>Step two, test the odd numbers one by one.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Twenty one is three times seven. Twenty five is five times five, and twenty seven is three times nine. These three are composite.
<bookmark mark='primes'/>Nothing except one and itself divides twenty three. The same holds for twenty nine, so these two are prime.

beats.on_screen: Check: 2 prime + 5 even + 3 odd composite = 10 numbers

marks.count: the counts are written under the strip
marks.total: the total of ten is written

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step three, check the count. Five even and three odd composite numbers make eight composite numbers.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Adding the two prime numbers gives ten, which matches the ten numbers we started with.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>From twenty one to thirty, two numbers are prime and eight are composite.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: all the odd numbers are prime, crossed out; 25 = 5 × 5 and 21 = 3 × 7

marks.doubt: Keeko's doubt appears in a bubble
marks.odd: twenty five and twenty one are shown with their factor pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks all the odd numbers are prime.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>But twenty five is five times five, and twenty one is three times seven. Each has more than two factors.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>An odd number can be composite, so we must look for a factor pair every time.
